newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi won't last full term - Bertinotti.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi won't last full term - Bertinotti.

text.p: The leader of Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation party said in an interview published on Sunday that he doubted whether Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government would last a full five-year term.
"It's highly improbable that the whole legislature will go ahead with this (ruling) majority and this government," La Repubblica newspaper quoted Fausto Bertinotti as saying.
"As things stand at the moment, this is unfortunately the realistic analysis."

Prodi, in office for 10 months, relies on Bertinotti's party for a majority in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house). The relationship has often been fractious, but Prodi has said there will be no change to the ruling majority.
Bertinotti conceded that the political climate had improved, but spelled out three big difficulties in the coming months.

The first was unemployment and privatisation, the second, Prodi's plans for a spring mini-budget to try to ensure that Italy is in shape to join a single European currency at the outset and the third, the full 1998 budget.
"A deal on the first two is difficult and nearly impossible on the third," Bertinotti said.
He has already told Prodi he cannot accept cuts in welfare spending or tax hikes in the forthcoming mini-budget package.
He told La Repubblica Prodi could raise revenue from a levy on severance pay.
Communist Refoundation's role supporting the government would only last as long as it was advantageous and "as long as in Italy the government avoids cuts in social spending."
"If it (the government) falls? Let it fall, what am I supposed to do about it?" Bertinotti said.
